commits.author: Joost VandeVondele <Joost.VandeVondele@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Fix shared memory recovery

Key the Unix server socket path by a process-local counter in addition to the PID, so that several SharedMemory instances in the same process cannot unlink each other's endpoints and make the segment undiscoverable to newly launched processes.

Accept WAIT_ABANDONED from WaitForSingleObject on Windows, which also grants ownership of the initialization mutex, and let the existing initialization flag determine whether the previous owner finished.

closes https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7333

No functional change
commits.subject: Fix shared memory recovery

commits.author: Carlos Esparza <ca2010es@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Fix static assert for constexpr Zobrist

Written on top of #7312, sorry that makes it harder to read. The static_assert from 54a85ce8f43ffe0204d332c352c7b43ec5f4803d is incorrect: For example, if all castling keys are set to zero then the `cr == 0` check in the continue will skip the iteration that should return false. The correct condition is `a == b` instead of `cr == 0`, which is what this patch does.

While I was at it I also replaced `int b = 0` with `int b = a` (and same for `f2`) since the cancellation check is symmetric in `a` and `b`.

closes https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7319

No functional change

commits.author: Elhamuddin <elhamuddinazizi607@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Simplify bestValue update condition in parent node futility pruning

The !is_decisive(bestValue) guard is redundant.

is_decisive is defined as is_win or is_loss. The pruning block in Step 15 only runs if !is_loss(bestValue), so the only way is_decisive(bestValue) could be true is if bestValue is a win score. The same condition requires bestValue <= futilityValue and !is_win(futilityValue), so bestValue can't be a win score either.

Thus, dropping the guard retains the bench signature.

closes https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7322

No functional change
commits.subject: Simplify bestValue update condition in parent node futility pruning

Use least significant bit of keys to store stm

The last bit of `Position::key()`, `Position::pawn_key()`, `::non_pawn_key()` and `::minor_piece_key()` now equals `::side_to_move()`. Consequently we no longer need to explicitly index the corresponding histories by stm. Also removes `Zobrist::noPawns` which was already redundant.

This might help with blundering already won games due to hash collisions, since the eval obtained will at least be for the correct side.

commits.author: SanityEclipse000 <maksym.nikbakht@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Prefetch next weight tile in accumulator updates

Prefetches the next tile of each weight row while the current tile is being added in the accumulator update. The tile loops walk all changed rows together and the hardware prefetcher doesn't keep up with that many rows.

Follow-up to #7287. Only compiled in where it helped:
- rows longer than two tiles, so not avx512 (my first version lost there)
- builds with fast pext, so not the avx2 build. zen 1/2 only get avx2 builds, and vondele measured #7287 at -1.85% on his 3950X (-0.16% with the pext gate, where it's the same code as master)
So avx2, avx512 and everything else compile to the same code as master, only bmi2 and avxvnni change.

Rebased on the accumulator rewrite, and dropped the end-of-row check as mstembera suggested (prefetch never faults), so no tile index gets passed around anymore.

commits.author: Timothy Herchen <timothy.herchen@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Unroll important loops

Historically we've had issues with compilers not unrolling loops in NNUE: https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/issues/6474 , https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7251

These loops are special in that not unrolling them is always extremely bad for performance, rather than a heuristic that the compiler should guide to balance code size and instruction count. Thus, for GCC and clang, introduce `UNROLLED_FOR` that unconditionally unrolls these loops.

commits.author: Shawn Xu <xu107288696@gmail.com>
commits.message:
Update NNUE architecture to SFNNv20 and net nn-18cd32e11a9c.nnue

Combination of two changes:
* An additional two keys to the LayerStack selection, factorized in training, that results in 192 unique configurations. The keys are
    * Whether pawns occupy the full board, one half, or none
    * Whether at least one side has >=2 non-pawn pieces (officers)
* Lower LR for non-factorizer K32Q2 and Threats input weights.

Both changes have been individually tested. Over half of the 192 LayerStack buckets are impossible to encounter in any reasonable game and are not present in learnable quantities in the training data. These buckets are dynamically pruned pre-training. QAT warmups were added to reduce the impact of init noise. It is not expected to bring any elo gain.

commits.author: Robert Nurnberg @ elitebook <28635489+robertnurnberg@users.noreply.github.com>
commits.message:
Fix final PV output when Skill Level is enabled

If Skill Level is enabled, master may not always show the correct final PV (and eval) corresponding to the chosen bestmove. This PR fixes this by setting `uciPvSent` to false if a swap of rootmoves took place.

Example:
```
setoption name Skill Level value 0
go depth 10
```
Master:
```
info depth 10 seldepth 11 multipv 1 score cp 23 nodes 13995 nps 424090 hashfull 2 tbhits 0 time 33 pv e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 d2d4 e5d4 f3d4
bestmove d2d3 ponder d7d5
```
Patch:
```
info depth 10 seldepth 11 multipv 1 score cp 23 nodes 13995 nps 311000 hashfull 2 tbhits 0 time 45 pv e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 d2d4 e5d4 f3d4
info depth 10 seldepth 10 multipv 1 score cp 18 nodes 13995 nps 311000 hashfull 2 tbhits 0 time 45 pv d2d4 g8f6 g1f3 d7d5 c2c4 c7c6 e2e3
bestmove d2d4 ponder g8f6
```

closes https://github.com/official-stockfish/Stockfish/pull/7267

No functional change
commits.subject: Fix final PV output when Skill Level is enabled
